scope: Independent Windows checkout bootstrap and CPU inference; not a new scientific performance experiment
initial_inputs: 10 local copies of public resources, independently checked against pinned SHA256
3 original best checkpoints packed into a local test ZIP

limitations.source_vs_publication_models: Both original checkpoints and the separately restored published model ZIP were tested. All 11 published policies loaded on CPU; 16-step contact and visual-DP trajectories exactly matched the corresponding original-checkpoint CPU runs.
limitations.runtime: Existing Python dependency environment reused; all scientific commands launched in new processes.

rule.success_criterion: coverage >= 0.95 at any executed state; native_success separately uses > 0.95
rule.compute_budget_note: Equal real action budget, not equal computation: contact controllers simulate candidates; direct policies do not.
rule.replanning_schedule: Replan after completing the queued approach, push and hold; executed states are observed every action.
rule.flow_record_note: NPZ desired_flow_world is recomputed from each observed state for diagnostics. Contact-score inputs are the frozen-at-replan flows stored in each JSON plan.
rule.future_leakage_guard: No trajectory data loaded. Planner uses current state and fixed goal only.
rule.observations: privileged simulator pose, fixed geometry, actual pusher xy; target-generated flow
rule.controller_note: 8 contact candidates x 2 push lengths, shared simulator-dynamics candidate model and visibility-graph paths; collision warm-start caches are rebuilt
